mainTopic: רבי and אנטונינוס's secret friendship, אנטונינוס's share in עולם הבא, and the story of קטיעה בר שלום
overview: This amud continues the stories of the Roman ruler אנטונינוס and his friend רבי יהודה הנשיא. First the גמרא explains why רבי answered אנטונינוס only with hints: he feared the Romans would hear, and even a whisper can get out. Then come stories of their secret friendship: coded messages using plant names, gold hidden under wheat, a secret tunnel, and רבי חנינא בר חמא reviving a dead servant. אנטונינוס humbly serves רבי and asks whether he will reach עולם הבא. רבי says yes and answers his challenges from פסוקים, and ברייתות back him up. A ברייתא names אנטונינוס and קטיעה בר שלום as non-Jews who are not among the doomed. The גמרא then tells how קטיעה argued against an emperor's plan to destroy the Jews. He was put to death for it, circumcised himself, and was declared ready for עולם הבא. The amud ends as רב begins his words on the death of אדרכן, which continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not just say it openly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי gave אנטונינוס a hidden, acted-out answer instead of saying his advice clearly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him just tell him openly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier story, where רבי answered אנטונינוס's question only with a silent hint. Why didn't he simply speak?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, רבי answered אנטונינוס's political question by acting out a sign instead of speaking. A hint like that can easily be misunderstood. So the גמרא asks why he took that risk.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him (a challenge: why didn't he?)

phrases.english: But let him say it to him openly!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier story, where רבי answered with a hint
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's choice to answer אנטונינוס with a silent hint
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A clear spoken answer would be easier to understand, so why use a hint?

steps.title: He feared the powerful Romans would hear
steps.stepSummary: רבי was afraid that important Romans would hear his advice and make trouble for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to himself: The important Romans will hear me and cause me pain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that speaking openly was dangerous. Important Romans might overhear and punish רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's advice touched on Roman politics. If powerful Romans heard a Jewish leader advising the emperor, they could harm him. A hint kept the message hidden from anyone listening in.

keyTerms.meaning: The important or powerful people of Rome
They will cause me pain or trouble

phrases.english: He said: They will hear me,
the important Romans, and they will cause me pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Speaking openly would have been the better choice
steps.terutzMaskana: Speaking openly was too dangerous because the Romans might overhear

steps.title: Then why not whisper it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: if he feared being overheard, why not say it quietly?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say it to him in a whisper!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. A whisper would solve the problem of being overheard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear of being overheard explains why רבי avoided speaking loudly. It does not explain why he avoided speaking at all, since whispering seems safe enough.

phrases.english: But let him say it to him in a whisper!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that fear of being overheard forced רבי to use a hint
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whispering would also prevent others from hearing, so the hint should not have been needed

steps.title: Even a whisper can get out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק teaching that even secret words somehow get spread around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: 'For a bird of the sky will carry the sound.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even whispered words can leak out. It proves this from a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק warns that even words said in private can reach the wrong ears, as if a bird carried them away. So only a silent hint was truly safe. This closes the question about why רבי used a hint.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is written (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי answered אנטונינוס with hints because both loud words and whispers could reach the Romans. Only a silent sign was safe.

phrases.english: Because it is written:
"For a bird of the sky will carry the sound."
phrases.notes: קהלת 10:20

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב: כִּי עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם יוֹלִיךְ אֶת הַקּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק that secrets leak
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A whisper is safe from being overheard
steps.terutzMaskana: Even whispered words get out, so only a silent hint was safe

steps.title: A coded talk with plants about אנטונינוס's daughter
steps.stepSummary: אנטונינוס and רבי trade plants whose names hint at a private message about his daughter גירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אנטונינוס had a daughter named גירא who did something forbidden. He sent רבי a rocket plant (hinting: she sinned). רבי sent back coriander (hinting: kill your daughter). אנטונינוס sent leeks (hinting: I will be cut off if I do). רבי sent lettuce (hinting: then have mercy on her).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story of the two speaking in code. This time they send each other plants whose names sound like words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each plant name hides a word. גַּרְגִּירָא hints she sinned. כּוּסְבַּרְתָּא hints 'kill the daughter.' כַּרָּתֵי hints 'I will be cut off.' חַסָּא hints 'have mercy.' The story fits the earlier point: sensitive matters were passed along only in hidden ways.
steps.confusionAlert: The plants are not real gifts of food. Each one is a message, and the meaning is in how its name sounds.

phrases.english: He had a certain daughter
whose name was Gira, who was doing a forbidden thing.
He sent him a rocket plant (gargira).
phrases.notes: The name hints at 'Gira sinned,' so this was his way of telling רבי what happened.

phrases.english: He sent him coriander (kusbarta).
phrases.notes: Heard as 'kill the daughter,' since she deserved death for what she did.

phrases.english: He sent him leeks (karti).
phrases.notes: Sounds like 'cut off,' meaning: if I kill her, I will be cut off.

phrases.english: He sent him lettuce (chasa).
phrases.notes: Sounds like 'have mercy,' so: then spare her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא בְּרַתָּא דִּשְׁמַהּ גִּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story showing the same habit of secret, coded messages
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנטונינוס and רבי passed private messages through plant names, ending with רבי advising mercy

steps.title: Gold hidden under wheat
steps.stepSummary: Every day אנטונינוס sent רבי sacks of gold, covered with wheat so his servants wouldn't know.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day he would send him crushed gold in big sacks, with wheat on top at the openings. He told his servants: Bring wheat to רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins another story about אנטונינוס's secret gifts to רבי. This step sets up רבי's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wheat on top hid the gold, so the servants thought they were only carrying wheat. Once again the friendship is kept secret.

phrases.english: Every day he would send him
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'send.'

phrases.english: crushed gold in large sacks,
with wheat at their openings.
He said to them: Bring wheat to Rebbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל יוֹמָא הֲוָה מְשַׁדַּר לֵיהּ דַּהֲבָא פְּרִיכָא בְּמַטְרָאתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about the secret friendship
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנטונינוס secretly sent רבי gold hidden under wheat every day

steps.title: The gold is for future generations
steps.stepSummary: רבי says he doesn't need the gold. אנטונינוס answers that it will help רבי's descendants in later times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to him: I don't need it; I have plenty. אנטונינוס said: Let it be for those after you, who will give it to the last ones who come after you. Those who come from them will bring it out and use it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי turns down the gold because he is already wealthy. אנטונינוס explains that the gift is really for the generations to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's refusal shows he was not taking gifts for his own gain. אנטונינוס looks ahead and says later generations will need this money, for example to pay what the Romans demand of them.

keyTerms.meaning: For those who come after you

phrases.english: Rebbi said to him: I don't need it,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: I have plenty.
He said: Let it be for those after you,
who will give it to the last ones who come after you,
and those who come from them will bring it out for their needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי: לָא צְרִיכְנָא, אִית לִי טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the gold story with רבי's response and אנטונינוס's reply
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי refused the gold for himself, and אנטונינוס said it was meant for future generations

steps.title: The secret tunnel to רבי's house
steps.stepSummary: אנטונינוס used a secret tunnel to visit רבי, and he went to extreme lengths so that no one would know about the visits.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had a tunnel that went from his house to רבי's house. Every day he would bring two servants. He killed one at the door of רבי's house and one at the door of his own house. He said to רבי: When I come, let no man be found with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells one more story showing how completely אנטונינוס hid his visits to רבי. He used a tunnel and made sure no witnesses were left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Killing the servants meant no living person could report the visits. He also asked רבי to have nobody present when he came. This strongly repeats the theme of the whole section: the friendship had to stay completely secret from the Romans.

keyTerms.meaning: A man before you, anyone with you

steps.whatToRemember: All these stories show the same thing: אנטונינוס and רבי were close friends, but everything between them had to be hidden from the Romans.

phrases.english: He had a certain tunnel
that went from his house to Rebbi's house.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל יוֹמָא הֲוָה מַיְיתֵי תְּרֵי עַבְדֵי,
phrases.english: Every day he would bring two servants.
One he would kill at the door of Rebbi's house,
and one he would kill at the door of his own house.
He said to him: At the time that I come,
let no man be found before you.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהִיא נְקִרְתָּא דַּהֲוָה עָיְילָא מִבֵּיתֵיהּ לְבֵית רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about the secret friendship
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנטונינוס visited רבי through a secret tunnel and left no witnesses

steps.title: אנטונינוס finds someone else in the room
steps.stepSummary: אנטונינוס finds רבי חנינא בר חמא with רבי and complains. רבי calms him, and אנטונינוס sends רבי חנינא to wake a servant.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day אנטונינוס found רבי חנינא בר חמא sitting there. He said: Didn't I tell you that when I come, no one should be with you? רבי said: This one is not an ordinary human. אנטונינוס then told רבי חנינא: Tell that servant sleeping at the gate to get up and come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. אנטונינוס's rule of total secrecy seems to have been broken. This story also sets up the miracle in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed how hard אנטונינוס worked so that no one would know about his visits. Here someone is actually in the room. רבי answers that this person is on such a high level that he is no danger at all.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time that I come
This one is not an (ordinary) human being

phrases.english: One day he found

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Ḥama, who was sitting there.
He said: Did I not tell you
that at the time that I come
no man should be found before you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֵית דֵּין בַּר אִינִישׁ.
phrases.english: He said to him: This one is not a human being.
phrases.notes: רבי means this is no ordinary person, so אנטונינוס has nothing to worry about.

phrases.english: He said to him: Tell
phrases.notes: Now אנטונינוס is talking to רבי חנינא בר חמא.

phrases.english: that servant who is sleeping at the gate
that he should get up and come.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the secrecy theme from step 8 by showing a moment when the secrecy seemed to be broken.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי assures אנטונינוס that רבי חנינא בר חמא is like no ordinary person, so his presence is no threat.

steps.title: רבי חנינא revives the dead servant
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא finds the servant dead. He is stuck on how to act, so he prays and brings the servant back to life. אנטונינוס is impressed but still insists on secrecy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא went and found the servant had been killed. He thought: What should I do? If I tell אנטונינוס he was killed, that is bad, because one does not bring bad news. If I leave and say nothing, I am disrespecting the king. So he prayed, brought the servant back to life, and sent him. אנטונינוס said: I know even the smallest among you can revive the dead. But still, when I come, no one should be with you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא is caught between two bad choices. He solves the problem by praying and reviving the servant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling the king about the death means bringing bad news. Ignoring the king's order means disrespecting the kingdom. Reviving the servant avoids both problems. אנטונינוס admits that even the least among the Jewish sages can revive the dead, but he still keeps his rule of total privacy.

keyTerms.meaning: One does not report bad news
I am treating the kingdom with disrespect
Bring the dead back to life

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Ḥama went,
he found that he had been killed.
phrases.notes: He means the servant at the gate.

phrases.english: He said: How should I act?
If I go and tell him that he was killed,
that is a problem, because one does not report bad news.
If I leave him and go,
I am treating the kingdom with disrespect.
He prayed for mercy on him
and brought him back to life and sent him.
He said: I know
phrases.notes: Now אנטונינוס is speaking.

phrases.english: that the smallest among you
can bring the dead back to life,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'revive.'

phrases.english: but at the time that I come
no person should be found before you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ דַּהֲוָה קְטִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 9, where אנטונינוס sent רבי חנינא to wake the servant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא avoids both bringing bad news and disrespecting the king by reviving the servant. אנטונינוס still keeps his demand for privacy.

steps.title: אנטונינוס humbly serves רבי
steps.stepSummary: אנטונינוס serves רבי every day and even offers to be a step to his bed. רבי objects, and אנטונינוס wishes he could be רבי's mattress in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day אנטונינוס served רבי, giving him food and drink. When רבי wanted to get into bed, אנטונינוס would bend down in front of it and say: Step on me to get into your bed. רבי said: It is not proper to disrespect the kingdom this much. אנטונינוס said: If only I could be a mattress under you in עולם הבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how deeply a Roman ruler humbled himself before רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי refuses because a king lowering himself this far is disrespect to the kingdom. אנטונינוס answers that he would gladly be even lower than that, as long as he could be close to רבי in עולם הבא. This sets up his question in the next step.

phrases.english: Every day he would serve Rabbi:
he would feed him and give him to drink.
When Rabbi wanted
to go up to bed,
he would bend down in front of the bed
and say to him: Go up on me to your bed.
He said to him: It is not proper conduct
to disrespect the kingdom this much.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי יְשִׂמֵנִי מַצָּע תַּחְתֶּיךָ
phrases.english: He said to him: If only I could be made a mattress under you
in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another story about אנטונינוס's devotion to רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנטונינוס's humility toward רבי was so great that he longed to be beneath him even in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Will אנטונינוס reach עולם הבא?
steps.stepSummary: אנטונינוס asks רבי whether he will enter עולם הבא, and רבי says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אנטונינוס said to רבי: Will I come to עולם הבא? רבי said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: אנטונינוס asks a direct question and gets a clear yes. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wish in step 11 to be near רבי in עולם הבא leads naturally to this question. רבי's simple 'yes' is what the next step will question.

phrases.english: He said to him: Will I come to the World to Come?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from אנטונינוס's wish about עולם הבא in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether אנטונינוס has a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: A verse says עשו's house will have no survivor
steps.stepSummary: אנטונינוס challenges רבי's answer with a פסוק saying that no one from the house of עשו will survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: אנטונינוס said: But isn't it written, 'There shall be no survivor of the house of עשו'?
steps.whatsHappening: אנטונינוס questions רבי's 'yes' by quoting a פסוק that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rome is traditionally linked with עשו, so as a Roman ruler, אנטונינוס sees himself as part of 'the house of עשו.' If that house will have no survivor, how can he have a share in עולם הבא?

phrases.english: He said to him: But isn't it written:
"There shall be no survivor of the house of Esau"!
phrases.notes: עובדיה 1:18

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב לֹא יִהְיֶה שָׂרִיד לְבֵית עֵשָׂו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's 'yes' from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's statement that אנטונינוס will enter עולם הבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says the entire house of עשו will have no survivor, and אנטונינוס belongs to that house.

steps.title: The verse means those who act like עשו
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains that the פסוק is only about people who do the deeds of עשו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי answered: The פסוק is talking about someone who does the deeds of עשו.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the challenge by narrowing who the פסוק is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is not about everyone descended from עשו or connected to him. It is about people who act wickedly like עשו did. אנטונינוס, who serves רבי with such humility, does not fit that description.

keyTerms.meaning: About one who does the deeds of עשו

steps.whatToRemember: A person's share in עולם הבא depends on how he acts, not on which nation he comes from. אנטונינוס, a Roman, has a share because he does not act like עשו.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי does not say אנטונינוס is not part of the house of עשו. He says the פסוק's punishment only applies to those who act like עשו.

phrases.english: It is talking about one who does the deeds of Esau.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק cuts off everyone belonging to the house of עשו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק cuts off only those who do the deeds of עשו.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up רבי's answer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same thing רבי said: the פסוק about no survivors for עשו's house refers only to those who do עשו's deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: 'There shall not be any survivor of the house of עשו.' You might think this means everyone. So the פסוק says 'of the house of עשו' to teach that it means only those who act like עשו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי told אנטונינוס in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 רבי limited the פסוק to people who do עשו's deeds. Now a ברייתא makes the same reading of the words 'house of עשו.' This shows רבי's answer is not a private opinion but an accepted teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא (a support formula)
Therefore the פסוק says (introduces the answer to a wrong assumption)
The deeds of עשו, acting the way עשו acted

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
"There shall not be any survivor of the house of Esau"
phrases.notes: עובדיה 1:18

phrases.english: One might think this applies to everyone?
So the verse says: "of the house of Esau,"
meaning one who does the deeds of Esau.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי's answer from step 14 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's reading that the פסוק only covers those who act like עשו
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the words 'לבית עשו' the same way

steps.title: אנטונינוס brings a פסוק about all the kings and leaders of אדום
steps.stepSummary: אנטונינוס challenges again with a פסוק that lists אדום, her kings, and all her leaders among the doomed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But isn't it written, 'There is אדום, her kings and all her leaders'?
steps.whatsHappening: אנטונינוס pushes back with a new פסוק that seems to include every king of אדום, which would include him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's earlier answer said only people who act like עשו are lost. But this פסוק seems to name the whole ruling class of אדום with no exceptions. As a Roman ruler, אנטונינוס worries he is included no matter what he does.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
אדום, the nation from עשו, identified with Rome

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here אנטונינוס is speaking to רבי.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"There is Edom, her kings and all her leaders"!
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 32:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי's answer, using a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's claim that אנטונינוס will reach עולם הבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to include all the kings and leaders of אדום, with no limit based on their deeds.

steps.title: רבי reads the פסוק as not including every king and officer
steps.stepSummary: רבי points out the exact wording: 'her kings,' not 'all her kings,' and 'all her leaders,' not 'all her officers.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It says 'her kings,' not 'all her kings.' It says 'all her leaders,' not 'all her officers.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers by reading the פסוק's words very carefully to show it does not include everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For kings, the word 'all' is missing, so not every king is included. For leaders, 'all' is written, but it says 'leaders' and not 'officers,' so it does not cover every officer. Either way, room is left for some to reach עולם הבא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
"Her kings" — but not "all her kings,"
"All her leaders" — but not "all her officers."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of the פסוק's exact wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק includes every king and leader of אדום.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording leaves out some kings and some officers, so they can still reach עולם הבא.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי and names the two exceptions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא makes the same reading and says who is left out: אנטונינוס among the kings and קטיעה בר שלום among the officers.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: 'Her kings,' not all her kings; 'all her leaders,' not all her officers. 'Her kings, not all her kings' leaves out אנטונינוס בן אסוירוס. 'All her leaders, not all her officers' leaves out קטיעה בר שלום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רבי's reading and names exactly who is excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats רבי's two readings word for word. Then it adds new information: the king left out is אנטונינוס himself, and the officer left out is קטיעה בר שלום. This directly answers אנטונינוס's worry about himself.

keyTerms.meaning: אנטונינוס son of Asveirus, the Roman ruler who was רבי's friend
קטיעה bar שלום, a Roman officer

steps.whatToRemember: Both פסוקים are read narrowly: only those who act like עשו are lost, and not every king or officer of אדום is included. אנטונינוס and קטיעה בר שלום are the named exceptions.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
"Her kings" but not "all her kings,"
"All her leaders" but not "all her officers."
"Her kings" but not "all her kings" —
this leaves out Antoninus son of Asveirus;
"All her leaders" but not "all her officers" —
this leaves out Ketia bar Shalom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי's answer in step 17 and adds the names of those excluded.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's narrow reading of 'her kings' and 'all her leaders'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads the פסוק the same way and names אנטונינוס and קטיעה בר שלום

steps.title: Who was קטיעה בר שלום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what happened with קטיעה בר שלום that earned him this special mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: קטיעה בר שלום, what was his story?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a background question to set up the story of קטיעה בר שלום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know who אנטונינוס is from the earlier stories, but קטיעה בר שלום is a new name. The גמרא wants to know what he did to be left out of the doomed officers of אדום.

phrases.english: Ketia bar Shalom, what was his story?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the background of the second name mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did קטיעה בר שלום do to deserve עולם הבא?

steps.title: The emperor's riddle about cutting off a sore
steps.stepSummary: The story begins: an emperor who hated the Jews asks his advisors whether a man with a sore on his foot should cut it off and live or leave it and suffer. They say cut it off.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an emperor who hated the Jews. He said to the important people of the kingdom: If someone has a sore growing on his foot, should he cut it off and live, or leave it and suffer? They said to him: He should cut it off and live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling the story of קטיעה בר שלום, beginning with the emperor's riddle to his advisors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The emperor speaks in a parable: the sore stands for the Jewish people, and cutting it off means destroying them. His advisors agree to cut it off. This sets the scene for what קטיעה בר שלום will do next.

keyTerms.meaning: The important people of the kingdom

steps.confusionAlert: The emperor is not really asking about medicine. The sore on the foot is his hidden way of talking about the Jews.

phrases.english: For there was a certain emperor
who hated the Jews.
He said to the important people of the kingdom:
Someone who has a sore growing on his foot,
phrases.notes: The sore is his way of hinting at the Jews.

phrases.english: should he cut it off and live,
or leave it and suffer?
They said to him: He should cut it off and live.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 19 by telling the story of קטיעה בר שלום.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The story starts with an emperor planning to destroy the Jews, using the parable of a sore that should be cut off.

steps.title: קטיעה's first argument: you cannot destroy them all
steps.stepSummary: קטיעה בר שלום rejects the advisors' 'cut it off' advice. His first reason is a פסוק showing the Jews cannot all be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: קטיעה בר שלום said to them: First, you cannot destroy all of them, as it is written: 'For like the four winds of the heavens I have spread you.'
steps.whatsHappening: קטיעה בר שלום speaks up against the advisors, who told the emperor to 'cut off the sore.' He starts with his first reason: a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The advisors compared the Jews to a sore foot that should be cut off. קטיעה answers that this plan cannot even work. The Jews are spread in a way that cannot be undone, and he brings a פסוק to show it.

keyTerms.meaning: A Roman official who stood up for the Jews

phrases.english: Ketia bar Shalom said to them:
One, that you cannot [destroy] all of them,
as it is written: 'For like the four winds of the heavens'
phrases.notes: זכריה 2:10

phrases.english: 'I have spread you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ קְטִיעָה בַּר שָׁלוֹם: חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the advisors' 'cut it off' advice from step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The advice to destroy the Jews
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is impossible to destroy all of them, according to the פסוק.

steps.title: What does 'like the four winds' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means. It suggests it means the Jews were scattered, then rejects that reading because of the wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the פסוק saying? If you say it means 'I scattered you to the four winds,' then instead of 'like the four winds' it should have said 'to the four winds'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the פסוק really means. It tests one reading and shows the wording does not fit it. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the meaning were 'scattered in all directions,' the פסוק should say 'to the four winds.' It actually says 'like the four winds,' which is a comparison. So the פסוק must be comparing ישראל to the winds in some way.

phrases.english: What is it saying?
If you say [it means] that I scattered you in the four directions,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets, and the corrected text has the square-bracket words instead. Both mean 'scattered.'

phrases.english: then this 'like the four winds' —
it should have said 'to the four winds'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the פסוק quoted in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'like the four winds' in the פסוק.

steps.title: The world cannot exist without ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The real meaning: just as the world needs winds, it needs ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, just as the world cannot exist without winds, so too the world cannot exist without ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true meaning of the פסוק. ישראל is compared to the winds, which the world cannot do without.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'like' points to a comparison. Winds are a lasting, necessary part of the world, and so is ישראל. That is why the emperor cannot destroy them.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Like the four winds' means ישראל is as necessary to the world as the winds are.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא רוּחוֹת,
phrases.english: Rather, just as the world cannot [exist] without winds,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: so too the world cannot [exist] without Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא רוּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק compares ישראל to the winds: the world cannot exist without either.

steps.title: קטיעה's second argument: Rome will be called the cut-off kingdom
steps.stepSummary: קטיעה adds a second reason: if Rome did this, people would call it 'the cut-off kingdom.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, they will call you 'the cut-off kingdom.'
steps.whatsHappening: קטיעה gives his second reason against the plan. It would bring shame on the empire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the advisors' own picture around. They said to cut off the sore on the foot. קטיעה says the result would be a 'cut-off' kingdom, a name of disgrace.

phrases.english: And furthermore, they will call you 'the cut-off kingdom.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason to the first one in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Destroying the Jews would shame Rome as a 'cut-off kingdom.'

steps.title: The emperor agrees but sentences קטיעה
steps.stepSummary: The emperor admits קטיעה is right, but says whoever beats the king in argument is thrown into a pit of ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have spoken well. But anyone who defeats the king is thrown into a pit of ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The emperor answers קטיעה. He admits the argument is correct, but punishes him anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The emperor does not dispute the reasoning. He only invokes a rule that anyone who wins against the king must die. So קטיעה's own victory costs him his life.

keyTerms.meaning: A hollow pit full of ashes (or a furnace)

phrases.english: He said to him: You have spoken well,
but anyone who defeats the king [in argument]
they throw him into a hollow pit of ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The emperor's response to קטיעה's two arguments.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is correct, but the speaker must die for defeating the king.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The emperor admits קטיעה is right but sentences him to death for defeating the king in argument.

steps.title: קטיעה circumcises himself on the way
steps.stepSummary: A noblewoman hints that he is going without 'paying the toll,' so קטיעה circumcises himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As they were taking him away, a certain noblewoman said to him: Woe to the ship that sails without paying the toll. He bent over, cut off his foreskin, and said: I have paid my toll; I will pass and cross over.
steps.whatsHappening: On the way to his death, קטיעה is told he is 'going without paying the toll.' He circumcises himself on the spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קטיעה was not circumcised. The woman's hint was about ברית מילה. He takes the hint and does it himself, saying he has now 'paid' and can cross into the next world.

phrases.english: As they were holding him and going,
a certain noblewoman said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וַוי לֵיהּ לְאִילְפָא דְּאָזְלָא בְּלָא מִכְסָא.
phrases.english: Woe to the ship that sails without [paying] the toll.
phrases.notes: The 'toll' is a hint about ברית מילה, as his next action shows.

phrases.english: He bent over the tip of his foreskin and cut it off,
[and] said: I have paid my toll; I will pass and cross over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the sentence of death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קטיעה circumcises himself before his death.

steps.title: קטיעה leaves his property to רבי עקיבא and his colleagues
steps.stepSummary: As he is thrown in, קטיעה gives all his property to רבי עקיבא and his colleagues.
steps.simpleTranslation: As they were throwing him in, he said: All my property goes to רבי עקיבא and his colleagues.
steps.whatsHappening: In his last moment, קטיעה gives away everything he owns to the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He names two parties: רבי עקיבא, and 'his colleagues.' This wording raises a question of how to split the property, which the next step answers.

phrases.english: As they were throwing him [in], he said:
All my property [goes] to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story to the moment of his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קטיעה's property is given to רבי עקיבא and his colleagues.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns: half to אהרן, half to his sons
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from a פסוק that 'to אהרן and his sons' means half and half. So he takes half, and his colleagues take half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went out and taught: 'And it shall be for אהרן and for his sons' means half for אהרן and half for his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא uses a פסוק to show how to divide a gift given to 'one person and his group.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names אהרן by himself and then his sons as a group. רבי עקיבא learns that the named person gets half and the group shares the other half. The same applies to 'רבי עקיבא and his colleagues.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went out and taught:
'And it shall be for Aaron and for his sons' —
phrases.notes: שמות 29:28

phrases.english: half for Aaron and half for his sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to divide the gift from step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gift to 'X and his group' is split: half to X, half to the group.

steps.title: A בת קול announces קטיעה's reward
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול declares that קטיעה בר שלום is ready for life in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said: קטיעה בר שלום is ready for life in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The story returns to קטיעה. A heavenly voice announces that he has earned עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the ברייתא in step 18 singled out קטיעה among the officers. He is not among the doomed, because Heaven itself declared his reward.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:

phrases.aramaic: קְטִיעָה בַּר שָׁלוֹם מְזֻומָּן לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: Ketia bar Shalom is ready for life in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to קטיעה's story after the side point about dividing the property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קטיעה בר שלום earned עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי weeps: some earn their world in one moment
steps.stepSummary: רבי cries and says some people earn their world in one moment, and others only after many years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי wept and said: There is one who acquires his world in one moment, and there is one who acquires his world over many years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי reacts to the story. This closes the story of קטיעה בר שלום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קטיעה earned עולם הבא through one act of courage at the end of his life. Others need a lifetime of work. רבי is moved by how much a single moment can be worth.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquires his world (his share in עולם הבא)

steps.whatToRemember: קטיעה בר שלום stood up for the Jews with his argument, gave his life, and earned עולם הבא in one moment. That is why he is excluded from the doomed 'officers.'

phrases.english: Rabbi wept and said:
There is one who acquires his world in one moment,
and there is one who acquires his world over many years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי's reaction to the בת קול.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One moment of greatness can earn עולם הבא, just like years of effort.

steps.title: אנטונינוס served רבי, and אדרכן served רב
steps.stepSummary: A new story: two non-Jewish rulers served great חכמים. When אנטונינוס died, רבי said 'the bundle is broken apart.' Then רב's reaction to אדרכן's death begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: אנטונינוס served רבי, and אדרכן served רב. When אנטונינוס died, רבי said: The bundle is broken apart. When אדרכן died, רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new short story pairing two rulers with two חכמים. It ends just as רב begins to speak, setting up his words in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's words 'the bundle is broken apart' express that a close bond ended with אנטונינוס's death. The parallel line about רב is set up here, but his actual words come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A Persian ruler who served רב

phrases.english: Antoninus served Rabbi,
[and] Adrakan served Rav.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שְׁכֵיב אַנְטוֹנִינוּס, אָמַר רַבִּי: נִתְפָּרְדָה חֲבִילָה.
phrases.english: When Antoninus died, Rabbi said: The bundle is broken apart.
When Adrakan died, Rav said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about אנטונינוס after the קטיעה story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנטונינוס served רבי, and רבי mourned his death as the breaking of a bond.
